== crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs#L116-L188
   116  usage: con-ron [--verified|--trusted] [--jobs=<n>] [--no-mark-persistent]
   117                 [--progress[=<stride>]] [--pins FILE|--no-pins]
   118                 FILE.ndjson
   119         con-ron --help
   120  
   121    --verified        the default, and the mode the main theorem is about: every
   122                      environment the fold accepts in this mode has a model in
   123                      every set theory (ConLeche.model_exists,
   124                      ConLeche/MainTheorem.lean), so a stream declaring a
   125                      theorem of type False is never accepted
   126                      (ConLeche.no_False_theorem_accepted).  What the port
   127                      proves is that same statement about THIS program's fold
   128                      (DESIGN.md §1); con-leche's file-level corollary
   129                      ConLeche.no_False_declaration, which covers the parse as
   130                      well, is con-ron's follow-up task #84 and is NOT yet
   131                      claimed here.
   132    --trusted         the unverified mode: the SAME checker bodies at the mode
   133                      with the certification-only work switched off.  An accept
   134                      in this mode is outside the theorem.
   135    --jobs=<n>        the check phase's worker count: <n> workers claim records
   136                      one at a time off a shared counter, and --jobs=1 runs the
   137                      plain loop with no counter and no result table.  The
   138                      verdict, and the declaration a rejection names, are the
   139                      same at every <n>: the results are walked in RECORD order,
   140                      so the first failing record in fold order is the one
   141                      reported.  Each worker reserves 1 GiB of address space for
   142                      its stack, so a run under `ulimit -v` needs 3x the
   143                      checker's resident set plus a gigabyte per worker; the
   144                      DEFAULT is one worker per hardware thread capped at 16 for
   145                      that reason (con-leche's uncapped default aborts on a
   146                      96-thread machine).  0 or a non-numeral is a usage error,
   147                      as in con-leche.
   148    --no-mark-persistent
   149                      ACCEPTED AND A NO-OP: the mark it turns off is a
   150                      Lean-runtime reference-counting device
   151                      (Runtime.markPersistent), and this program's counts are
   152                      std::sync::Arc counts -- atomic by type, in every lane,
   153                      with no runtime mark to clear.  A run that passes it says
   154                      so on stderr.
   155    --progress[=<stride>]
   156                      opt-in progress heartbeat on STDERR, one line shape per
   157                      phase:
   158                        con-ron: parse done: <N> fold records ... t=<s>s
   159                        con-ron: install <i>/<N> <decl> t=<s>s
   160                        con-ron: install done: <N>/<N> ..., <M> checks pending t=<s>s
   161                        con-ron: check <done>/<M> <kind> <name> t=<s>s
   162                        con-ron: check done: <M>/<M> t=<s>s
   163                        con-ron: done: parse <p>s, install <i>s, check <c>s, <n> workers
   164                      An install line is printed BEFORE every <stride>-th
   165                      declaration is installed (<i> is its FOLD position, which
   166                      the stream's record index sits near but not at a fixed
   167                      offset above), so a run that dies in the install phase
   168                      names the declaration it died in on its last line.  A
   169                      check line is printed AFTER every <stride>-th COMPLETED
   170                      check.  On a failure the phase's closing line says so
   171                      ('install failed at', 'check failed at') and the summary
   172                      still prints.  Bare --progress is stride 1; a stride that
   173                      is not a decimal numeral, or 0, is a usage error.
   174    --pins FILE       con-ron's own, FOR TESTING: read the pin list from a
   175                      `con-ron-pins/1` dump instead of the core's own embedded
   176                      text (task #43), through the UNVERIFIED reader.
   177    --no-pins         con-ron's own, FOR TESTING: the empty pin list, the pin
   178                      loop's `[]` arm, under which a Nat.div/Nat.mod stream
   179                      declines.  Neither flag is needed for a normal run: the
   180                      pins are con-leche's `natOpPinSets`, embedded in the
   181                      verified core and decoded by it.
   182    --help            print this text on STDOUT and exit 0, in any argument
   183                      position; no input is read.
   184  
   185  Any other option is a usage error: the run reports it, prints this text and
   186  exits 3 without reading its input.
   187  
   188  exit codes: 0 accepted, 1 rejected, 2 declined, 3 usage/malformed/internal.

== scripts/setup-aeneas-lean.sh#L1-L14
     1  #!/usr/bin/env bash
     2  # Produce `_tmp/aeneas-lean/`: a copy of `vendor/aeneas/backends/lean` with
     3  # `patches/aeneas-433.patch` applied, so that the Aeneas Lean library
     4  # builds on con-leche's toolchain (leanprover/lean4:v4.33.0 + Mathlib v4.33.0).
     5  # See DESIGN.md, task #2.
     6  #
     7  # Idempotent: a stamp records the patch's and the source tree's hashes; a
     8  # second run with nothing changed is a no-op and, crucially, keeps the
     9  # existing `.lake/` (rebuilding Mathlib's dependents costs minutes).
    10  #
    11  # Exits non-zero if the patch does not apply cleanly to the pinned Aeneas
    12  # submodule -- that is the signal that the submodule moved and the patch needs
    13  # rebasing.
    14  #

   431      let df: u64 = data(&f);
   432      let da: u64 = data(&a);
   433      let h: u64 = hash32(name::mix_hash(
   434          17,
   435          name::mix_hash(hash_of_data(df), hash_of_data(da)),
   436      ));

   438          h,
   439          max_u64(bvar_of_data(df), bvar_of_data(da)),

== crates/con-ron-core/src/cached/core_c.rs#L5086-L5117
  5086  pub fn whnf_core(
  5087      mode: &CheckMode,
  5088      fuel: u64,
  5089      st: &mut CState,
  5090      fe: &FEnv,
  5091      d: u64,
  5092      e: &Expr,
  5093  ) -> CheckM<Expr> {
  5094      const M: [u32; 24] = [
  5095          102, 117, 101, 108, 32, 101, 120, 104, 97, 117, 115, 116, 101, 100, 58, 32, 119, 104,
  5096          110, 102, 67, 111, 114, 101,
  5097      ];
  5098      if fuel == 0 {
  5099          Err(core_types::internal(core_types::code_points(&M)))
  5100      } else {
  5101          match whnf_core_probe(st, e) {
  5102              Some(r) => Ok(r),
  5103              None => match whnf_core_body_i(mode, fuel - 1, st, fe, d, e) {
  5104                  Err(err) => Err(err),
  5105                  Ok(r) => {
  5106                      st.whnf_core_c.insert(expr::dup(e), expr::dup(&r));
  5107                      Ok(r)
  5108                  }
  5109              },
  5110          }
  5111      }
  5112  }

  1328  pub fn decode(t: &[u8]) -> CheckM<Vec<NatOpPinSet>> {
  1329      let hdr = pins_header();
  1330      if !starts_with_from(t, &hdr, 0) {
  1331          Err(bad_text())
  1332      } else {
  1333          run_records(t, hdr.len(), tables_new())
  1334      }
  1335  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/cached/checker_c.rs#L123-L132
   123  pub fn or_else_step(attempt: CheckM<bool>) -> OrElseStep {
   124      match attempt {
   125          Ok(true) => OrElseStep::Matched,
   126          Ok(false) => OrElseStep::Continue,
   127          Err(e) => match e {
   128              CheckError::Native(m) => OrElseStep::Failed(CheckError::Native(m)),
   129              _ => OrElseStep::Recovered(e),
   130          },
   131      }
   132  }

== proof/ConRon/Refine/State.lean#L640-L671
   640  structure StateRel (st : cached.state_c.CState)
   641      (lst : ConLeche.Cached.CState) : Prop where
   642    ienv : HashMap.RelOn NameWF st.ienv lst.ienv absName absCConstE
   643    constTyAt : HashMap.RelOn NameLevelsWF st.const_ty_at lst.constTyAt
   644      absNameLevels absExpr
   645    constValAt : HashMap.RelOn NameLevelsWF st.const_val_at lst.constValAt
   646      absNameLevels absExpr
   647    ruleRhsAt : HashMap.RelOn NameNameLevelsWF st.rule_rhs_at lst.ruleRhsAt
   648      absNameNameLevels absExpr
   649    whnfCoreC : HashMap.RelOn ExprWF st.whnf_core_c lst.whnfCoreC absExpr absExpr
   650    whnfC : HashMap.RelOn ExprWF st.whnf_c lst.whnfC absExpr absExpr
   651    inferC : HashMap.RelOn ExprWF st.infer_c lst.inferC absExpr absExpr
   652    inferIOC : HashMap.RelOn ExprWF st.infer_io_c lst.inferIOC absExpr absExpr
   653    defeqC : HashMap.RelOn ExprPairWF st.defeq_c lst.defeqC absExprPair id
   654    annotC : HashMap.RelOn ExprWF st.annot_c lst.annotC absExpr absExpr
   655    lsimpC : HashMap.RelOn LevelWF st.lsimp_c lst.lsimpC absLevel absLevel
   656    lnzC : HashMap.RelOn LevelWF st.lnz_c lst.lnzC absLevel id
   657    eqvC : HashMap.RelOn LevelPairWF st.eqv_c lst.eqvC absLevelPair id
   658    instC : HashMap.RelOn InstKeyWF st.inst_c lst.instC absInstKey absExpr
   659    /-- The `instC` table's **entry count**, which the other thirteen clauses do
   660    not need: `StateRel` is a lookup agreement and a lookup agreement does not
   661    bound the Lean map's size.  `cached::state_c::inst_list_m` is the one
   662    operation that reads a count — the `instC` entry cap, `inst_c.len() <
   663    inst_c_cap_c` against `mp.size < instCCapC` (`StateC.lean:186-199`) — so
   664    without this clause the two sides can disagree about whether the table is
   665    full.  Task #61 folded it in (`Refine/StateC.lean` had it as a free-standing
   666    `InstCSize` hypothesis that nothing could discharge). -/
   667    instCSize : (HashMap.al_v st.inst_c).length = lst.instC.size
   668  
   669  /-- The port-side invariant of the fourteen tables: each is a well-formed
   670  `ron::HashMap` (task #16's `Inv`) holding only well-formed keys and — where the
   671  values are terms — only well-formed values. -/

    96  def FEnvRel (fe : fenv.FEnv) (lfe : ConLeche.FEnv) : Prop :=
    97    absEnv fe.env = lfe.env ∧
    98    fe.visible_below.val = lfe.visibleBelow ∧
    99    HashMap.RelOn NameWF fe.idx lfe.idx absName absIdxEntry
   100  
   101  /-- The hereditary invariant of an `FEnv`. -/
   102  structure FEnvWF (fe : fenv.FEnv) : Prop where
   103    env : EnvWF fe.env
   104    inv : HashMap.Inv name.Name.Insts.Con_ron_coreRonHashmapHashable fe.idx

== proof/ConRon/Refine/Abs.lean#L511-L525
   511  inductive ExprWF : expr.Expr → Prop where
   512    | bvar {i e} : expr.bvar i = ok e → ExprWF e
   513    | fvar {idx ty e} : ExprWF ty → expr.fvar idx ty = ok e → ExprWF e
   514    | sort {u e} : LevelWF u → expr.sort u = ok e → ExprWF e
   515    | mk_const {n us e} : NameWF n → LevelsWF us → expr.mk_const n us = ok e → ExprWF e
   516    | app {f a e} : ExprWF f → ExprWF a → expr.app f a = ok e → ExprWF e
   517    | lam {ty b m e} : ExprWF ty → ExprWF b → BinderMetaWF m →
   518        expr.lam ty b m = ok e → ExprWF e
   519    | forall_e {ty b m e} : ExprWF ty → ExprWF b → BinderMetaWF m →
   520        expr.forall_e ty b m = ok e → ExprWF e
   521    | let_e {ty v b e} : ExprWF ty → ExprWF v → ExprWF b →
   522        expr.let_e ty v b = ok e → ExprWF e
   523    | lit {l e} : LiteralWF l → expr.lit l = ok e → ExprWF e
   524    | proj {s i x e} : NameWF s → ExprWF x → expr.proj s i x = ok e → ExprWF e
   525  

== proof/ConRon/Refine/Core/Arms/Shape.lean#L102-L119
   102  def SimS {α β : Type} (A : α → β) (WF : α → Prop)
   103      (f : cached.state_c.CState →
   104        Result ((core.result.Result α core_types.CheckError) × cached.state_c.CState))
   105      (g : ConLeche.Cached.CheckCM β) : Prop :=
   106    ∀ st o st', StateWF st → f st = Aeneas.Std.Result.ok (o, st') →
   107      ∀ lst, StateRel st lst → Out A WF o st' (g.run lst)
   108  
   109  /-- The same with the environment threaded: `Refine/FEnv.lean`'s `FEnvRel`
   110  relates the Rust `FEnv` to con-leche's, and con-leche reads it only through
   111  `find?`/`findProj?`. -/
   112  def Sim {α β : Type} (A : α → β) (WF : α → Prop)
   113      (f : cached.state_c.CState → fenv.FEnv →
   114        Result ((core.result.Result α core_types.CheckError) × cached.state_c.CState))
   115      (g : ConLeche.FEnv → ConLeche.Cached.CheckCM β) : Prop :=
   116    ∀ fe lfe, FEnvWF fe → FEnvRel fe lfe → SimS A WF (fun st => f st fe) (g lfe)
   117  
   118  /-- The pure shape: a Rust computation that touches neither state nor
   119  environment is a plain equation against its con-leche value. -/

   895  theorem knot_induction {mode : env.CheckMode}
   896      (harms : ∀ fuel, Wrappers mode fuel → Bodies mode fuel) (fuel : Std.U64) :
   897      KnotSpec mode fuel := by
   898    have key : ∀ n : Nat, ∀ f : Std.U64, f.val = n → Wrappers mode f := by
   899      intro n
   900      induction n with
   901      | zero =>
   902        intro f hfv
   903        have h0 : f = 0#u64 := u64_val_inj (by rw [hfv]; rfl)
   904        subst h0; exact wrappers_zero mode
   905      | succ n ih =>
   906        intro f hfv
   907        have hlt : n < 2 ^ Std.UScalarTy.U64.numBits := by
   908          have h1 : f.val < 2 ^ Std.UScalarTy.U64.numBits := f.bv.isLt
   909          omega
   910        have hg : (Std.UScalar.ofNatCore n hlt : Std.U64).val = n :=

    80  structure IndRoutesSpec (mode : env.CheckMode) : Prop where
    81    /-- **Route A, the fixpoint install** (`inductives_c::check_native_s`
    82    against `ConLeche.Cached.checkNativeS`, `Cached/CheckerC.lean:213-226`):
    83    when `native_parts::native_parts` recognises the block, con-leche's
    84    `nativeParts?` recognises it too, and the route agrees on the recognised
    85    parts. -/
    86    native : ∀ (st : cached.state_c.CState) (fe : fenv.FEnv)
    87        (n_p : Std.U64) (block : alloc.vec.Vec env.ConstantInfo)

    91      ConstantInfosWF block →
    92      inductives.native_parts.native_parts n_p block = ok (some p) →
    93      inductives.inductives_c.check_native_s mode st fe p = ok (.Ok fe', st') →
    94      ∀ lst lfe, StateRel st lst → FEnvRel fe lfe →
    95        ∃ lst' lfe' lp,
    96          ConLeche.nativeParts? n_p.val (absConstantInfos block) = some lp
    97          ∧ (ConLeche.Cached.checkNativeS (absMode mode) lfe lp).run lst = .ok (lfe', lst')
    98          ∧ StateRel st' lst' ∧ StateWF st' ∧ FEnvRel fe' lfe' ∧ FEnvWF fe'
    99          ∧ FEnvCanon fe' ∧ FEnvFull fe'
